title: Process deficiencies can coexist with a valid platform reason and no restoration remedy
source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/105
geography: Australia; comparative case used to test procedural fairness, remedy, and recovery stages in the US-centered atlas

filing_extension_granted.unit: extension granted and matter allowed to proceed

merits_outcome_observed.unit: merits outcome not yet available at this stage

observations.method: Case-level extraction from the official Fair Work Commission timing decision and the later merits decision.
observations.uncertainty: The timing decision establishes procedural continuation, not unfairness, restoration, payment, or later worker outcome.
observations.subgroup: One named platform worker whose application proceeded after a filing extension.
observations.counterinterpretation: A matter being allowed to proceed does not imply that the underlying deactivation was unlawful or that a remedy will follow.

valid_safety_reason_accepted.unit: safety complaints accepted as a valid reason for deactivation

observations.method: Case-level extraction from the official Fair Work Commission merits decision.
observations.uncertainty: The merits decision does not establish later account status, continued work, alternative work, payment, recurrence, trust, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Same named worker case after procedural continuation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A process defect can be insufficient for restoration where the decision-maker accepts a substantive safety reason; procedural quality and merits fairness are separate stages.

denominator.unit: same named worker case and official search route

payment_observed.unit: public payment or compensation record located

later_access_or_work_observed.unit: public later account-access or work record located

alternative_or_exit_observed.unit: public alternative-work, switching, non-use, or exit record located

observations.method: Targeted official Fair Work Commission public-document search for the later remedy and implementation outcome.
observations.uncertainty: Public non-observation cannot establish that private work, payment, account status, or later choice did not occur.
observations.subgroup: Same named worker case after merits dismissal.
observations.counterinterpretation: A dismissed unfair-deactivation claim is not evidence of no burden or no later consequence; it only limits what the public adjudicated record establishes about remedy.

related_sources.claim: Bounded case recheck preserving timing, process, merits, payment, access, alternatives, and exit stages.

boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It distinguishes filing continuation, process deficiency, substantive valid reason, unfairness finding, restoration, payment, later access, alternatives, trust, and exit.
